p.src: After the Mid-Autumn Festival had passed, Lady Wang saw that Xifeng's illness had abated somewhat. Though she was not yet fully recovered, she could now go about, so Lady Wang continued to have the physician take her pulse and prescribe medicine each day; he also wrote out a prescription for pills to regulate her courses and restore her vitality. As the prescription called for two ounces of the finest ginseng, Lady Wang had the stores searched. After half a day's rummaging, only a few roots no thicker than hairpins were found in a little box. Lady Wang inspected them and found them inferior. She ordered another search, which turned up a large packet of rootlets and scraps. Growing impatient, Lady Wang said, “When we have no use for a thing, it is always here; the moment we need it, it is nowhere to be found. I am forever telling you to go through everything and gather it all together in one place. But you never listen and simply toss things down wherever you happen to be. You do not understand how valuable it is. When it is needed, no matter how much money one spends on a replacement, the new stuff is still no good.” Caiyun said, “I expect it is all gone. This is the only lot left. Last time, the lady from the other household came asking for some, and you gave it all to her.” “Even if you think there is none,” said Lady Wang, “look again carefully.” Caiyun had no choice but to search again. She returned with several packets of medicinal ingredients and said, “We do not know what these are. Please inspect them yourself, madam. Apart from these, there is nothing else.” Lady Wang opened the packets, but she too had forgotten what medicines they contained, and there was not a single ginseng root among them. She therefore sent someone to ask whether Xifeng had any. Xifeng sent word back: “I have only a little ginseng extract, some root crowns, and fine roots. There are a few whole roots, but they are not of the finest quality, and I still need them for my daily decoction.” On hearing this, Lady Wang could only send to inquire of Lady Xing. Lady Xing replied, “When ours ran out last time, we came to you for some; what we received was used up long ago.” At her wits' end, Lady Wang had to go in person and ask Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia promptly ordered Yuanyang to bring out what remained from before. There was, remarkably, still a large packet of roots, all as thick as a finger, so she weighed out two ounces for Lady Wang. Lady Wang came out and handed it to Zhou Rui's wife, telling her to have a page deliver it to the physician's house. She also ordered her to take along the several unidentified packets, have the physician identify them, and return with each one labelled.

p.src: Presently Zhou Rui's wife brought the packets back and said, “They have all been wrapped separately and labelled with their names. As for this packet of ginseng, it was unquestionably of the finest quality—nowadays even thirty times its weight in silver would not buy its equal—but it is far too old. This substance is unlike other things. However fine it may be, once a hundred years have passed, it crumbles into ash of its own accord. Though this has not yet turned to ash, it has already become like rotten, decayed wood and has lost all medicinal potency. The physician asks you to put this away and obtain some fresh ginseng instead. Thick or thin, it does not much matter, provided it is new.” Lady Wang lowered her head and said nothing. Only after a long while did she say, “There is no help for it, then. We shall simply have to buy two ounces.” She had no inclination to inspect the other medicines and merely ordered, “Put them all away.” Then she told Zhou Rui's wife, “Go and tell the men outside to procure two ounces of the best they can find. If the Old Lady should happen to ask, simply say that we used hers; there is no need to tell her anything more.” Just as Zhou Rui's wife was about to leave, Baochai, who was seated there, smiled and said, “Wait a moment, Aunt. None of the ginseng sold outside nowadays is any good. Even when the dealers have a whole root, they are sure to cut it into two or three pieces and attach root crowns, pithy swellings, and rootlets, mixing everything together to make it easier to sell, so its original thickness cannot be judged. Our shops regularly deal with the ginseng merchants. I shall go and speak to Mother now, and have my brother send a clerk to explain matters to them and ask them to supply two ounces of fine, whole, unworked roots. It will do no harm to spend a few extra ounces of silver if it means obtaining something good.” Lady Wang smiled. “You certainly understand these matters. I am sorry to trouble you, but it would be best if you went there yourself.” Baochai accordingly left. She returned some time later and said, “Someone has been sent. We should have an answer by this evening. It will not be too late to have the medicine prepared first thing tomorrow morning.” Lady Wang was naturally delighted and said, “As the saying goes, ‘The oil-seller's wife dresses her hair with water.’ We have always had the finest ginseng at home, yet there is no telling how much of it we have given away. Now that we need some ourselves, we have ended up begging for it from every quarter.” With that, she heaved a long sigh. Baochai smiled. “Though ginseng is valuable, it is, after all, only medicine; it ought by rights to be distributed among those who need it and used to help people. We are not like families who know nothing of the world and, once they acquire such a thing, hoard it away as a precious treasure.” Lady Wang nodded. “What you say is perfectly right.”

p.src: After Baochai had gone, Lady Wang, seeing no one else in the room, summoned Zhou Rui's wife and asked whether anything had come of the search conducted in the Garden the other day. Zhou Rui's wife had already settled upon a course of action with Xifeng and the others, so she reported everything to Lady Wang without concealing a single detail. Lady Wang was both shocked and angry when she heard, yet found herself in a difficult position. Since Siqi belonged to Yingchun's household, and they were all people from the other branch of the family, she could only send someone to inform Lady Xing. Zhou Rui's wife replied, “The other day, the lady over there was angry with Wang Shanbao's wife for meddling and slapped her several times. Now she is pretending to be ill at home and refuses to take the lead. Besides, the girl is her own granddaughter. Having brought humiliation upon herself, she can only pretend to have forgotten the matter and wait until it has blown over before saying anything more. If we go over and report it now, I fear the lady may take it the wrong way and think that we are the ones meddling. It would be simpler to take Siqi straight over there and show the lady both the culprit and the evidence. At worst she will have the girl beaten, marry her off, and send another maid in her place. If we merely send word now, the lady over there may raise objection after objection and say, ‘If that is so, your mistress ought to deal with it herself. Why come and tell me?’ Would that not delay matters instead? And if the girl should seize an opportunity to kill herself, that would make matters worse. We have watched her for two or three days now, but everyone lets their guard down sometimes. If no one happens to be there at a critical moment, might that not lead to trouble?” Lady Wang thought for a moment and said, “That is true. Deal with this matter quickly, and then we shall deal with those little devils in our own household.” Upon hearing this, Zhou Rui's wife gathered the other married servants and first went to Yingchun's rooms. She told her, “The ladies have said that Siqi is grown now. Her mother has repeatedly petitioned them, and they have granted her mother's request to marry the girl off. She is to leave today, and another good maid will be chosen to serve you.” With that, she ordered Siqi to prepare to leave. Tears filled Yingchun's eyes, and she seemed reluctant to part with her. The previous night, however, she had heard other maids whispering about what had happened. Though it was hard to give up the affection of many years, the matter concerned propriety and morals, and there was nothing she could do. Siqi had already pleaded with Yingchun, truly hoping that her mistress would defend her to the utmost and obtain her pardon. But Yingchun was slow of speech, easily swayed by others, and irresolute, so she was incapable of making decisions for herself. Seeing this, Siqi knew that she could not escape her fate and cried, “How heartless you are, miss! You kept reassuring me these past two days, yet now why will you not say even a single word?” Zhou Rui's wife and the others said, “Do you still expect your young mistress to keep you? Even if she did, you would hardly be able to face anyone in the Garden. Take our well-meant advice: stop making such a scene and leave quickly and quietly, without anyone being the wiser. That way everyone can preserve some dignity.”

p.src: With tears in her eyes, Yingchun said, “I know what a grave wrong you have committed. If I were still to plead insistently to keep you, would that not be the ruin of me as well? Look at Ruhua: she had served here for years too, yet when they said she must go, she was gone. Naturally, it will not end with just the two of you. I expect all the older maids in this Garden will have to leave. As I see it, everyone must part in the end, so it is better that each of you should go your own way.” Zhou Rui's wife said, “That is why, after all, you are the sensible one, miss. There are others to be dismissed tomorrow, so set your mind at ease.” Siqi had no alternative. In tears, she kowtowed to Yingchun and bade farewell to the other girls. Then she whispered in Yingchun's ear, “If you hear that I am to be punished, please, for mercy's sake, put in a word for me, in remembrance of our years as mistress and servant!” Yingchun, also in tears, promised, “Do not worry.” Zhou Rui's wife and her companions then led Siqi out of the courtyard and ordered two old serving-women to carry all her belongings for her. They had gone only a few steps when Xiujú came hurrying after them from behind. Wiping away her own tears, she handed Siqi a silk-wrapped bundle and said, “This is from our young mistress. You have been mistress and servant all these years, and now you must suddenly part. Keep this as a remembrance of her.” When Siqi took it, she could not help bursting into fresh tears, and she and Xiujú wept together for a while. Zhou Rui's wife grew impatient and kept urging them on, so the two had no choice but to part. Siqi then pleaded through her tears, “Aunties, please show me a little kindness. Let us stop for a moment so that I may bid farewell to the girls I am closest to. After all, we have been good friends for several years.” Zhou Rui's wife and the others all had duties of their own and were undertaking this task only because they had no choice. Moreover, they deeply resented the haughty airs these girls habitually put on. They had no time now to listen to her, and sneered, “I advise you to keep moving and stop dragging your feet. We still have proper business to attend to. Which of them came crawling out of the same bundle of clothes as you? Why bid them farewell? They cannot get enough of laughing at you as it is. You are merely trying to put off the inevitable for another moment. Do you imagine the matter will be dropped if you delay long enough? Take my advice and be quick about it.” Even as she spoke, she did not slacken her pace but led Siqi straight out through the rear side gate. Helpless and afraid to say anything more, Siqi could only follow them out.

p.src: Just then Baoyu happened to come in from outside. Seeing Siqi being taken away and people following behind with bundles of her belongings, he knew that once she left she would never return. He had heard what had happened the previous night, and Qingwen's illness had also worsened after the events of that day. Though he questioned Qingwen closely, she would not tell him why. Only the day before he had seen Ruhua sent away, and now Siqi too was leaving. Feeling as though his soul had deserted him, he hurriedly barred her way and asked, “Where are you going?” Zhou Rui's wife and the others all knew Baoyu's usual ways and feared that his interference would delay matters. They therefore laughed and said, “This is none of your concern. Go and study.” Baoyu said with a smile, “Good sisters, please wait a moment. I have something sensible to say.” Zhou Rui's wife replied, “Madam will not permit even a moment's delay. What argument could you possibly have? We know only that we must obey Madam's orders; nothing else is our concern.” When Siqi saw Baoyu, she caught hold of him and wept, “They have no authority to decide. You must go and plead with Madam for me, whatever happens.” Baoyu too could not help grieving. With tears in his eyes he said, “I do not know what terrible thing you have done. Qingwen is ill, and now you are leaving too. If everyone is to leave, what am I to do?” Losing her temper, Zhou Rui's wife said to Siqi, “You are no longer a deputy young mistress. If you refuse to obey, I shall beat you. Do not imagine that, as in the past, your young mistress will shield you and let you make all the trouble you please. The more we speak to you, the more you refuse to go. What sort of decorum is this, tugging and clinging to a young master?” Without allowing any further protest, the married servants seized Siqi and dragged her away. Baoyu dared not say more for fear that they would carry tales against him. He merely glared at them in fury, and only when they had gone far away did he point after them and exclaim bitterly, “How extraordinary! How extraordinary! Why is it that the moment these people marry and become tainted with the smell of men, they turn so utterly vile—more hateful even than men themselves?” The old women guarding the garden gate could not help laughing when they heard him. One asked, “By that reasoning, are all maidens good and all married women bad?” Baoyu nodded. “Exactly, exactly!” The old women laughed. “There is one more thing we cannot make sense of, and we should like to ask you about it.” Just as they were about to speak, several other old women came over and said hurriedly, “Be careful, all of you. Summon everyone and have them ready to attend. Madam herself has come into the garden and is inspecting the servants over there. I fear she may inspect this place as well. She has also ordered that Miss Qingwen's elder brother and sister-in-law be fetched at once to wait here and take his sister away from Happy Red Court.” Then she laughed and said, “Amitabha Buddha! Heaven has opened its eyes today and is sending this plague-bearing enchantress away. Now we can all enjoy a little peace.”

p.src: As soon as Baoyu heard that Lady Wang had come to conduct an inspection, he knew that Qingwen too was doomed. He had already flown off in all haste, and so never heard this last malicious expression of satisfaction. When Baoyu reached Happy Red Court, he found a crowd gathered there. Lady Wang was seated inside with anger written all over her face, and she ignored him when he entered. For four or five days Qingwen had taken neither food nor water and lay weak and listless, scarcely breathing. Now she had been dragged down from the kang, her hair dishevelled and her face begrimed, and two women had only just managed to support her as they carried her away. Lady Wang ordered that only the clothes Qingwen was wearing be thrown out with her; her other good garments were to remain behind for deserving maids to wear. She also ordered every maid in the court to be summoned so that she might inspect them one by one. It turned out that after Lady Wang had lost her temper that day, Wang Shanbao's wife had seized the opportunity to denounce Qingwen. Others in the household who were at odds with people in the garden had likewise taken advantage of the occasion to add a few accusations. Lady Wang had stored every word in her memory. Since the festival had kept her occupied, she had restrained herself for two days; today she had come expressly to inspect the servants in person. Qingwen alone might not have mattered so much. More seriously, someone had raised the issue of Baoyu, saying that now he was grown and understood the relations between men and women, he had been corrupted by the shameless maids in his rooms, who had taught him such things. As this charge was even graver than the matter of Qingwen alone, Lady Wang personally examined every one of them, from Xiren down to the youngest little maids who performed rough chores. Then she asked, “Which one of you shares Baoyu's birthday?” The girl herself dared not answer, but an old nurse pointed her out. “This is Huixiang, who is also called Si'er. Her birthday is the same day as Baoyu's.” Lady Wang scrutinized her. Though she was not half as beautiful as Qingwen, she had a certain fresh and delicate charm. Her every movement openly displayed her cleverness, and she was dressed in a manner unlike the others. Lady Wang sneered. “Here is another shameless creature. She has been saying in private that people born on the same day are destined to be husband and wife. Did you say that? You imagined that because I live far away, I knew nothing of it. You should know that although I seldom come here in person, my thoughts, ears, and attention are always fixed upon this place. Baoyu is the only son I have. Do you suppose I would simply stand by and let you seduce and corrupt him?” When Si'er heard Lady Wang repeat the private words she had often exchanged with Baoyu, she could not help blushing. She lowered her head and shed tears. Lady Wang immediately ordered that her family be summoned at once to take her away and marry her off. Then she asked, “Which one is Yelü Xiongnu?” The old nurses pointed out Fangguan. Lady Wang said, “A girl who performed in the opera is naturally a little vixen! When you were released from service last time, you were too reluctant to leave. All the more reason, then, for you to have behaved yourself and kept to your proper place. u.src: As soon as Baoyu heard that Lady Wang had come to conduct an inspection, he knew that Qingwen too was doomed. He had already flown off in all haste, and so never heard this last malicious expression of satisfaction.
When Baoyu reached Happy Red Court, he found a crowd gathered there. Lady Wang was seated inside with anger written all over her face, and she ignored him when he entered.

For four or five days Qingwen had taken neither food nor water and lay weak and listless, scarcely breathing. Now she had been dragged down from the kang, her hair dishevelled and her face begrimed, and two women had only just managed to support her as they carried her away.

She also ordered every maid in the court to be summoned so that she might inspect them one by one.

It turned out that after Lady Wang had lost her temper that day, Wang Shanbao's wife had seized the opportunity to denounce Qingwen. Others in the household who were at odds with people in the garden had likewise taken advantage of the occasion to add a few accusations.
Lady Wang had stored every word in her memory.
Since the festival had kept her occupied, she had restrained herself for two days; today she had come expressly to inspect the servants in person.

You should know that although I seldom come here in person, my thoughts, ears, and attention are always fixed upon this place.

Then she asked, “Which one is Yelü Xiongnu?”

p.src: Fangguan smiled and protested, “I would never dare to put anyone up to anything.” Lady Wang smiled. “Still talking back, are you? p.src: Now, Baoyu had supposed that Lady Wang had merely come to conduct a search and that nothing serious would happen; never had he imagined that she would descend upon them in such thunderous fury. Every accusation concerned things said in their daily life and was accurate to the last word, so he knew there could be no reversing the decision. Though in his heart he wished he could die, with Lady Wang in such a rage he dared neither say another word nor make a single move, but accompanied her all the way to the Qinfang Pavilion. Lady Wang ordered him, “Go back and study your books properly. Take care, for I shall question you tomorrow. I have already sworn that I will.” Only after hearing this did Baoyu turn back. As he walked, he pondered, “Who could have carried such tales? Besides, no outsider knew what went on here. How could she have described everything so exactly?” Still thinking, he came inside and saw Xiren there shedding tears. The finest of them had been driven away—how could he not be heartbroken? He threw himself upon the bed and began to weep as well. Xiren knew that he could bear the other losses, but that Qingwen mattered more to him than anything. She nudged him and tried to console him: “Crying will do no good now. Sit up and listen to me. Qingwen is well again, and now that she has gone home, she can rest quietly for a few days. If you truly cannot bear to part with her, wait until Madam's anger has subsided, then appeal to the Old Lady. It should not be difficult to have her gradually brought back. Madam merely happened to believe someone's slander and acted this way in a moment of anger.” Baoyu cried, “I still cannot understand what monstrous crime Qingwen has committed!” Xiren replied, “Madam merely thought her too beautiful and therefore somewhat frivolous. Madam is firmly convinced that someone as beautiful as she is could never be well behaved, and that is why she detests her. Clumsy, plain girls like us are more to her liking.” Baoyu said, “Let that pass. But how did she learn of the private jokes among us? No outsider was here to let the secret slip. That is truly strange.” Xiren said, “You never exercise any restraint. Once you become excited, you pay no attention to whether anyone is present. I have given you warning looks and secret signals, but others noticed them while you yourself remained oblivious.” Baoyu said, “If Madam knows everyone else's faults, why did she single out neither you nor Sheyue nor Qiuwen?” At these words, Xiren's heart gave a start. She lowered her head for a long while, unable to answer, then smiled and said, “That is true. Come to think of it, we too have sometimes been careless and reckless in our joking. How could Madam have forgotten that? Perhaps she still has other matters to attend to and will deal with us when they are finished. One never knows.” Baoyu laughed. “You are famously the most virtuous and worthy of all, and those two have been molded and instructed by you. How could any of you have behaved recklessly enough to deserve punishment? It is only that Fangguan is still young and a little too clever; she cannot help using her advantage to overwhelm others, and that makes people dislike her.

p.src: I was the one who brought about Si'er's ruin. It began that year, on the day you and I quarreled, when I called her up here to do some light work. She inevitably took someone else's place, and that is why this has happened today. But Qingwen, like you, was brought up from childhood in the Old Lady's apartments. Though she was prettier than most, she never stood in anyone's way. She was merely frank by nature and rather sharp-tongued; after all, she had never offended any of you. I suppose she was simply too beautiful, and her beauty proved her undoing.” When he had finished, he began to weep again. Xiren pondered his words closely and sensed that Baoyu seemed to suspect her. She therefore dared not offer any more consolation, but sighed, “Heaven alone knows the truth. There is no way to discover the culprit now, and crying for a while will do no good. You would do better to preserve your strength and, when the Old Lady is in a good humor, explain everything clearly to her and ask to have Qingwen back. That is the proper course.” Baoyu gave a cold laugh. “There is no need to comfort me with empty hopes. By the time Madam has calmed down and we can judge the moment right to ask for her back, who knows whether her illness will wait that long? She has been tenderly raised and indulged since childhood; when has she ever suffered a single day of hardship? Even I, who understand her temperament, have often managed to offend her. Sending her away like this is like taking a pot of orchids that has only just put forth tender shoots and setting it down in a pigsty. Besides, she is gravely ill and has a heart full of pent-up anguish. She has neither a loving father nor a devoted mother, only a maternal cousin as loathsome as a drunken loach. Once she gets there, she will not be used to the place at all. How could she possibly last even a few days? Who knows whether I shall ever see her even once or twice more!” As he spoke, his grief deepened still further. Xiren smiled. “This is truly a case of ‘the magistrate may burn down houses, but the common people may not even light a lamp.’ If one of us happens to say the least inauspicious thing, you call it ill-omened talk; yet now you freely curse her yourself, and apparently that is perfectly proper! Even if she is somewhat more delicate than others, matters cannot be as dire as that.” Baoyu said, “I am not cursing her recklessly. There was already an omen this spring.” Xiren hastily asked what omen he meant. Baoyu said, “That perfectly healthy crab apple beneath the steps suddenly died on one side for no reason. I knew then that something strange was going to happen, and sure enough the omen has been fulfilled in her.” Hearing this, Xiren laughed again and said, “I mean to keep quiet, but I simply cannot contain myself. You are altogether too sentimental and fussy. How can such words come from a scholarly young gentleman like you? How can plants and trees possibly be connected with human lives? If this is not sentimental fussing, then you truly have become a fool.” Baoyu sighed. “What do any of you understand? Not only plants and trees, but everything beneath heaven possesses feeling and reason, just as people do; and when such a thing finds one who truly understands it, its responses can be extraordinarily miraculous.

p.src: To take great examples, there are the juniper before the Temple of Confucius, the yarrow at his grave, the cypress before Zhuge Liang's shrine, and the pine at the grave of Yue Wumu. All of these openly and honorably share in the righteous spirit of the people with whom they are associated. They are things whose glory has remained untarnished through the ages. They wither when the realm is in turmoil and flourish when it is well governed; over the course of hundreds and thousands of years, they have died and revived several times. Are these not omens and responses? For lesser examples, there are Yang Taizhen's tree peonies at the Pavilion of Aloes, the Love-longing Tree by the Tower of Upright Beauty, and the grass upon Wang Zhaojun's tomb. Did these not also give miraculous signs? Thus this crab apple likewise foretold that the person corresponding to it was about to die, and so half of it died first.” Hearing this foolish discourse, Xiren found it both laughable and lamentable. She said with a laugh, “Truly, the more you say, the angrier you make me. What sort of person is that Qingwen, that you should spend so much thought on her and compare her with all these worthy figures? Besides, however good she may be, she cannot take precedence over me. Even if this crab apple were to represent someone, it ought to represent me first; her turn would not yet have come. I suppose it is I who am going to die.” At these words, Baoyu hurriedly covered her mouth with his hand and urged her, “Why must you do this? One matter is not yet settled, and now you begin talking like this too. Enough. Let us speak no more of it, lest, after losing three of them, I should lose yet another as well.” Hearing this, Xiren was secretly delighted and thought, “If I had not spoken so, you would never have let the matter rest.” Baoyu then said, “From now on, let us not mention it again. We shall simply regard all three of them as dead; that is all there is to it. After all, people have died before, and you have not seen anything happen to me. That is one way of looking at it. For now, let us attend to what can still be done: without concealing it from those below, but keeping it from our superiors, we should quietly send someone to take her belongings out to her. And if we have any money saved from our usual allowances, we should take out a few strings for her medical care. That would be fitting after all the affection between you sisters.” Xiren laughed. “You take us for people who are both petty and heartless. There was no need to wait for you to say this. I have already gathered together all the clothes she ordinarily wore, along with every one of her other belongings, and put them over there. There are too many people and prying eyes about in daylight, and I am afraid of causing trouble. We shall wait until evening and quietly have Nanny Song carry them out to her. I also have a few strings of cash saved up, and I shall give those to her too.” On hearing this, Baoyu thanked her profusely. Xiren laughed. “I have long been renowned as a paragon of virtue. Surely I know how to purchase at least this little bit of a good name!” Remembering what she had said earlier, Baoyu hastened to smile ingratiatingly and soothe her for a while. That evening, as promised, they secretly sent Nanny Song to deliver the things. After putting everyone at ease, Baoyu seized an opportunity to slip alone through the rear side gate and begged an old serving woman to guide him to Qingwen's home to see her.

Qingwen had originally been bought for silver by the Lai household; she was only ten then and had not yet begun to grow her hair long. As she often accompanied Granny Lai on visits, Grandmother Jia saw how clever and pretty she was and became extremely fond of her. Granny Lai therefore presented her to Grandmother Jia as a servant, which was how she later came to Baoyu’s apartments. When Qingwen entered the household, she could no longer remember her native place or her parents. She knew only that she had a maternal cousin skilled at butchery who had likewise fallen on hard times outside the household, so she asked the Lais to buy him too and bring him in as a hired servant. The Lais saw that although Qingwen now served before Grandmother Jia and was exceptionally quick-witted, sharp-tongued, and high-spirited, she had not forgotten old ties. They therefore bought her cousin and gave him one of their servant girls as his wife. Once married and comfortably settled, however, her cousin forgot the days when he had wandered destitute. He drank himself senseless whenever he pleased and took no care of his household. Worse still, he had married a beautiful and amorous wife. Seeing him careless of his own health, insensible to romance, and intent only on drinking himself insensible, she could not help lamenting that a reed had been propped beside jade and grieving that her beauty languished alone. They were now Qingwen’s only relatives, and so, after being expelled, she had come to their home.

p.src: At that moment Duo Hunchong was out, and Miss Deng had gone visiting after her meal. Qingwen alone remained, lying prone in the outer room. Baoyu told the old woman to keep watch outside the courtyard gate. Entering alone, he lifted the straw curtain and at once saw Qingwen lying on the earthen kang covered with a reed mat; fortunately, her quilts and bedding were still those she had used before. He had no idea what he ought to do. Tears in his eyes, he went up, gently took hold of her, and softly called her twice. Qingwen had caught a chill and had also endured cruel words from her cousin and his wife. Her illness had worsened; after coughing all day, she had only just fallen into a fitful sleep. Suddenly hearing someone call her, she forced open her bright eyes. When she saw it was Baoyu, shock, joy, sorrow, and pain swept over her, and she seized his hand in a desperate grip. She choked with sobs for a long while before she could utter even half a sentence: “I thought I would never see you again.” Then she began coughing without cease. Baoyu too could do nothing but choke back his sobs. Qingwen said, “Amitabha! Thank heaven you have come. Pour me half a bowl of that tea to drink. p.src: Before he had finished speaking, her sister-in-law came in smiling and lifted the curtain. “Well, well! I heard everything you two said.” Then she turned to Baoyu. “What is a young master like you doing in a servant’s room? Seeing that I am young and pretty, have you perhaps come to flirt with me?” Baoyu was so frightened by this that he hurriedly smiled and pleaded, “Dear sister, please do not speak so loudly. She served me faithfully, so I slipped out to see how she was.” Miss Deng took Baoyu by the hand and led him into the inner room. Smiling, she said, “Keeping me quiet is easy enough, provided you grant me one request.” As she spoke, she sat down on the edge of the kang and clasped Baoyu tightly in her arms. Baoyu had never encountered anything like this. His heart began pounding; his whole face flushed with agitation, and, mortified and afraid, he could only say, “Dear sister, please stop teasing me.” Miss Deng gave him a sidelong look through her tipsy eyes and laughed. “Pooh! I am forever hearing that you are an old hand at amorous games. Why have you suddenly turned bashful today?” Baoyu blushed and said with a smile, “Please let go of me, sister. Whatever you have to say, we can discuss it properly. There are old women outside. What would they think if they heard us?” Miss Deng laughed. “I came in some time ago and sent the old woman to wait by the garden gate. I have been longing and longing, and today I have finally caught you. But fame is no substitute for meeting a man in person. For all your handsome looks, you are nothing but a firecracker without powder—fit only for show. Why, you are even shyer and more bashful than I am. It only shows that nothing people say can be trusted. Take just now, when our girl came here: I was certain that the two of you had long been carrying on in secret. I came in and listened carefully beneath the window for a while. There were only the two of you inside, and if you had been carrying on together, surely it would have come up in your talk. Yet, to my surprise, neither of you had ever trespassed upon the other. There must be no shortage of unjust accusations in this world. Now I regret having misjudged you both. Since that is how matters stand, you may set your mind at ease. Come whenever you please from now on, and I will not make trouble for you.” Only then did Baoyu feel reassured. He rose, straightened his clothes, and pleaded, “Dear sister, please take especially good care of her for the next two days. I must go now.” With that, he went back out and told Qingwen as well. Naturally, neither could bear to part from the other, but part they must. Knowing how hard it was for Baoyu to leave, Qingwen covered her head with the quilt and refused to respond to him at all; only then did Baoyu go out. He meant to visit Fangguan and Si’er as well, but it was already dark, and he had been away for quite some time. Fearing that those inside might notice his absence and that further trouble might arise, he returned to the garden for the present, resolving to make other plans the next day. When he reached the rear side gate, the pages were already carrying in the bedding and the matrons inside were checking everyone’s presence. Had he been one step later, the gate would have been shut.

p.src: Baoyu entered the garden, glad that no one had noticed. On reaching his own quarters, he merely told Xiren that he had been at Aunt Xue’s, and the matter ended there. When it was time to make the beds, Xiren had no choice but to ask how the sleeping arrangements were to be made that night. “Arrange it however you like,” Baoyu replied. During the past year or two, since Lady Wang had begun to hold Xiren in high regard, Xiren had become increasingly mindful of her own dignity. Whenever they were alone, especially at night, she avoided all intimacy with Baoyu, and the two had actually grown more distant than when they were younger. Moreover, though she had no great affairs to manage, the sewing and all matters concerning money, clothing, footwear, and other articles coming in or going out for Baoyu and the young maids were exceedingly tedious. Her old illness of coughing blood had healed, but whenever toil, wind, or cold affected her, blood would again appear in her sputum. For this reason, she had lately ceased altogether to sleep in Baoyu’s room at night. Baoyu often woke during the night and was extremely timid; whenever he woke, he invariably called for someone. Since Qingwen slept lightly and moved quickly, every nighttime duty—bringing tea or water, helping him sit up, and answering his calls—had been entrusted to her alone. Thus it was always Qingwen who slept on the outer bed beside Baoyu’s. Now that she was gone, Xiren had to ask what was to be done, for she knew this duty was more important than any performed during the day. Since Baoyu had answered that he did not care how they arranged matters, Xiren had no choice but to follow the custom of former years. She moved her own bedding back and laid it outside his bed. Baoyu sat in a daze throughout the evening. After they urged him to bed and Xiren and the others had also lain down, they heard him sighing again and again upon his pillow, tossing this way and that until after the third watch. Only then did he gradually settle down, and soon a faint snore could be heard. Xiren’s mind was at last at ease, and she too drifted into a light sleep. Before enough time had passed to drink half a cup of tea, she heard Baoyu call, “Qingwen!” Xiren hurriedly opened her eyes, answered him several times, and asked what he wanted. Baoyu wanted some tea. Xiren quickly got down, dipped her hands in the basin, poured half a cup of tea from the warming pot, and brought it for him to drink. Baoyu then smiled and said, “I have grown so used to calling her lately that I forgot it was you.” Xiren laughed. “When she first came, you used to call my name constantly in your sleep as well. It took half a year before you changed. I know that although Qingwen herself is gone, the two syllables of her name will not so easily depart.” After this, they both lay down again. Baoyu tossed and turned for another watch. Just as he finally fell asleep at the fifth watch, he saw Qingwen enter from outside, looking exactly as she had before. She came in and smiled at him. “Take good care of yourselves. From this moment, I am leaving you forever.” With that, she turned and left. Baoyu cried out after her and woke Xiren once more. Xiren assumed he had merely called out from force of habit, but then she saw that Baoyu was weeping. “Qingwen is dead,” he said. Xiren laughed. “What can you mean by saying such a thing! You do nothing but talk nonsense. What would people think if they heard you?”

p.src: But Baoyu would not listen; he wished daylight would come at once so that he could send someone to ask for news. At daybreak, a young maid from Lady Wang's quarters was already waiting for the front corner gate to be opened, bearing this message from her mistress: “Wake Baoyu at once. Have him wash his face, change his clothes, and come quickly. Someone has invited the master to enjoy the autumn scenery and admire the cassia blossoms today. Since the master was pleased with the fine poems he composed the other day, he intends to take the boys along.” “Those are Her Ladyship's very words; do not get a single word wrong. Run and tell him at once. Have him come immediately—the master is still waiting in the main apartments to have flour gruel with him. Brother Huan is already here. Run, quickly! Send someone else to summon Brother Lan, and give him exactly the same message.” The old women inside acknowledged each sentence as they heard it, fastening their buttons while opening the gate. Meanwhile, two or three of them were already fastening their clothes as they hurried off in different directions. Hearing a knock at the courtyard gate, Xiren knew that something was afoot. She hurriedly ordered someone to inquire, while she herself was already getting up. When she heard the message, she had someone fetch warm washing water and urged Baoyu to rise and wash. She herself went to fetch his clothes. Knowing that he was going out with Jia Zheng, she would not bring out any of his particularly splendid new clothes or shoes. She chose only articles of middling quality. Baoyu had no choice and came hurrying over. Sure enough, Jia Zheng was there drinking tea in excellent spirits. Baoyu promptly performed his morning obeisance. Jia Huan and Jia Lan also exchanged greetings with Baoyu. Jia Zheng told them to sit and take tea, then said to Huan and Lan, “Baoyu is not so good at his studies as you two, but when it comes to the quick wit needed for matching couplets and composing verse on a set theme, neither of you is his equal. On today's outing you will doubtless be pressed to compose poems, so Baoyu must help the two of you whenever necessary.” Lady Wang and the others had never heard Jia Zheng pass such a judgment before, and it came as a truly unexpected delight.

p.src: After Jia Zheng and the boys had gone and Lady Wang was about to visit Grandmother Jia, the foster mothers of Fangguan and the other two came in and reported, “Ever since Your Ladyship graciously released Fangguan the day before yesterday, she has behaved like a mad creature, taking neither tea nor food. She has drawn Ouguan and Ruiguan into it as well, and all three threaten to kill themselves, insisting on cutting off their hair and becoming nuns. “I thought that, being children, they were merely unaccustomed to living outside and would recover in a couple of days. But instead their disturbance grows worse, and even beatings and scoldings do not frighten them. We truly can do nothing with them, so we have come to beg Your Ladyship either to let them become nuns as they wish, or to discipline them and give them to someone else as daughters. We have not the good fortune to keep them.” Lady Wang exclaimed, “Nonsense! “They cannot simply do as they please. Do they imagine that anyone may enter the Buddhist order so lightly? Give each of them a beating, and see whether they still make such a commotion!” Now it was customary on the fifteenth day of the eighth month to send offerings to the various temples and for nuns from those temples to bring back the tips of the offerings. On the fifteenth Lady Wang had asked Zhitong of Water Moon Convent and Yuanxin of Ksitigarbha Convent to stay for two days, and they had not yet left. Hearing this news, they were only too eager to lure away two more girls to work for them, and both said to Lady Wang, “Yours is indeed a household of charitable people. “Because Your Ladyship delights in good works, your virtue has inspired all these young girls to feel as they do. Though it is true that entrance into the Buddhist order is not lightly gained, one must also remember that the Buddha's Law regards all beings equally. Our Buddha vowed to save all living creatures, even chickens and dogs; the only trouble is that those sunk in delusion will not awaken. If one possesses roots of goodness and can awaken, one may escape the cycle of rebirth. Indeed, the scriptures record many tigers, wolves, snakes, and insects that attained enlightenment. These two or three girls have neither fathers nor mothers, and their homes are far away. They have tasted wealth and splendor, yet they remember the hardship of their childhood and how they entered this profession of beauty and entertainment. Who knows what fate awaits them for the rest of their lives? To turn back from the sea of suffering, leave the world, and cultivate merit for their next existence is therefore a noble aspiration on their part. Your Ladyship should not obstruct their virtuous intention.” Lady Wang was naturally charitable. At first she had refused to let the girls do as they pleased because she considered Fangguan and the others mere children who had conceived this notion in a moment of disappointment; she feared that later they would be unable to endure the austere life and would only bring sin upon themselves. But now the two nuns' words seemed quite reasonable. Moreover, there had lately been many troubles in the household: Lady Xing had sent word that she would take Yingchun home the next day for a two-day stay so that a prospective family might inspect her, and an official matchmaker had come to discuss a marriage for Tanchun. Lady Wang's mind was in turmoil, and she had little attention to spare for such trifles.

They have tasted wealth and splendor, yet they remember the hardship of their childhood and how they entered this profession of beauty and entertainment. Who knows what fate awaits them for the rest of their lives? To turn back from the sea of suffering, leave the world, and cultivate merit for their next existence is therefore a noble aspiration on their part.
Your Ladyship should not obstruct their virtuous intention.”

Lady Wang was naturally charitable. At first she had refused to let the girls do as they pleased because she considered Fangguan and the others mere children who had conceived this notion in a moment of disappointment; she feared that later they would be unable to endure the austere life and would only bring sin upon themselves.

But now the two nuns' words seemed quite reasonable. Moreover, there had lately been many troubles in the household: Lady Xing had sent word that she would take Yingchun home the next day for a two-day stay so that a prospective family might inspect her, and an official matchmaker had come to discuss a marriage for Tanchun. Lady Wang's mind was in turmoil, and she had little attention to spare for such trifles.

p.src: Having heard this, she smiled and replied, “Since you two speak so persuasively, why not take them away as your disciples?” The two nuns invoked the Buddha and cried, “Excellent! “Excellent! “If that is so, the hidden merit Your Ladyship will earn is truly great.” With that, they bowed their heads to the ground in thanks. Lady Wang said, “In that case, go and ask them. “If they are truly sincere, let them come here and formally acknowledge you as their teachers in my presence before they leave.” The three women went out upon hearing this and duly brought the three girls in. Lady Wang questioned them repeatedly, but all three had made up their minds. They therefore kowtowed to the two nuns and then bowed farewell to Lady Wang. Seeing how resolute they all were, Lady Wang knew that they could not be compelled otherwise. Feeling sorrow and pity for them instead, she promptly ordered some things to be brought as further gifts for the girls and also presented the two nuns with gifts. From then on, Fangguan followed Zhitong to Water Moon Convent, while Ruiguan and Ouguan followed Yuanxin to Ksitigarbha Convent, and each left the world to become a nun.
